subject: physiology
title: Parathyroid Hormone, Calcitriol, and Phosphate Balance

steps.tx: Serum calcium exists in three distinct physiological fractions: forty-five percent is bound to plasma proteins (predominantly albumin), ten percent is complexed with citrate and phosphate, and fifty percent circulates as **serum ionised calcium**. Only the unbound ionised calcium fraction is biologically active and tightly regulated.
steps.say: Only free ionised calcium is biologically active, representing fifty percent of total serum calcium.

rows: Biologically active; regulates PTH and neuromuscular excitability

steps.tx: Because hydrogen ions compete with calcium for negatively charged binding sites on serum albumin, acute acid-base disturbances shift the ionised calcium fraction. In acute respiratory alkalosis, hydrogen ions dissociate from albumin, increasing negative charges that bind free calcium, precipitating acute **symptomatic hypocalcaemic tetany**.
steps.say: Alkalosis increases calcium binding to albumin, dropping free ionised calcium and triggering tetany and muscle cramps.

nodes.label: Acute Hyperventilation Lowers Arterial PaCO2, Raising Blood pH (Alkalosis)
Protons Dissociate from Albumin Imidazole Rings into Plasma to Buffer pH
Unmasked Negative Charges on Albumin Avidly Bind Circulating Free Ca2+
Ionised Calcium Plummets: Voltage-Gated Na+ Channels Excite, Eliciting Tetany

steps.tx: Chief cells of the parathyroid glands monitor extracellular ionised calcium continuously through cell-surface **calcium-sensing receptors**. Operating via Gq and Gi proteins, receptor activation by elevated extracellular calcium increases intracellular calcium and lowers cyclic AMP, which uniquely and potently inhibits parathyroid hormone secretion.
steps.say: Calcium-sensing receptors on chief cells detect high calcium and shut off parathyroid hormone secretion.

left.title: Hypocalcaemic State (< 1.15 mmol/L)
points: Calcium-sensing receptor (CaSR) remains unbound and inactive
Adenylyl cyclase disinhibited; intracellular cyclic AMP climbs
Triggers robust exocytosis of pre-formed parathyroid hormone granules
Stimulates parathyroid cell proliferation over days to weeks

right.title: Hypercalcaemic State (> 1.30 mmol/L)
points: High extracellular Ca2+ binds and activates Gq/Gi-coupled CaSR
Intracellular IP3 and calcium surge; adenylyl cyclase inhibited
Directly suppresses pre-formed PTH exocytosis within seconds
Stimulates degradation of stored PTH inside chief cells

steps.tx: Secreted by chief cells, **parathyroid hormone** is an eighty-four amino acid linear polypeptide that acts on bone and kidneys to elevate serum calcium while lowering serum phosphate. In proximal renal tubules, parathyroid hormone internalizes sodium-phosphate cotransporters, producing marked phosphaturia to prevent calcium phosphate precipitation.
steps.say: Parathyroid hormone raises blood calcium and lowers phosphate by causing profound renal phosphate excretion.

nodes.label: Parathyroid Chief Cells Secrete Active PTH in Response to Hypocalcaemia
Binds Gs-Coupled PTH1R Receptors in Proximal Renal Convoluted Tubules
Endocytic Internalization and Degradation of Apical NaPi-2a Cotransporters
Massive Phosphaturia Eliminates Phosphate, Lowering Serum Phosphate Product

steps.tx: In the distal convoluted tubule, parathyroid hormone stimulates active calcium reabsorption through apical TRPV5 channels and basolateral sodium-calcium exchangers. Simultaneously, parathyroid hormone transcriptionally upregulates the renal mitochondrial enzyme **one-alpha-hydroxylase**, catalyzing the final activation step of twenty-five-hydroxyvitamin D into fully active hormonal calcitriol.
steps.say: In the kidney, PTH reabsorbs calcium and activates the one-alpha-hydroxylase enzyme to synthesize calcitriol.

steps.tx: Synthesized in the skin via ultraviolet photolysis of seven-dehydrocholesterol or ingested in the diet, cholecalciferol undergoes sequential two-step enzymatic hydroxylation. The liver performs initial twenty-five-hydroxylation via CYP2R1, followed by proximal renal tubular **one-alpha-hydroxylation of vitamin D** to generate active one-alpha-twenty-five-dihydroxycholecalciferol to stimulate calcium absorption.
steps.say: Vitamin D is hydroxylated first in the liver, and then in the kidney by one-alpha-hydroxylase into active calcitriol.

steps.tx: Synthesized by parafollicular C cells of the thyroid gland, the thirty-two amino acid peptide **calcitonin** acts as a physiological antagonist to parathyroid hormone. Secreted in response to acute hypercalcaemia, calcitonin directly binds calcitonin receptors on mature osteoclasts, rapidly inactivating them to halt osteocytic bone resorption.
steps.say: Calcitonin is secreted by thyroid C cells in hypercalcaemia, directly shutting down osteoclasts to lower blood calcium.

left.title: Parathyroid Hormone (PTH)
points: Secreted by parathyroid chief cells in response to hypocalcaemia
Increases serum calcium; decreases serum phosphate (phosphaturic)
Essential for life; surgical removal produces fatal tetany

right.title: Calcitonin
points: Secreted by thyroid parafollicular C cells in hypercalcaemia
Decreases serum calcium and phosphate by inhibiting osteoclasts
Physiological role in adults is minor; used pharmacologically in Paget disease
Serves as a premier tumor marker for medullary thyroid carcinoma

steps.tx: Autonomous hypersecretion of parathyroid hormone by a single benign parathyroid adenoma causes **primary hyperparathyroidism**. Characterized by the classic mnemonic of painful bones, renal stones, abdominal groans, and psychiatric moans, patients exhibit hypercalcaemia, hypophosphataemia, hypercalciuria, elevated alkaline phosphatase, and osteitis fibrosa cystica.
steps.say: Primary hyperparathyroidism causes hypercalcaemia, hypophosphataemia, recurrent kidney stones, and osteitis fibrosa cystica.
